column1: # SoN::Verify's counts per rule per source, 2026-11-19: `tools/wire-verify.pl --tsv`
# fails if a rule's count RISES above its row here, or `#wires` falls below it.
# Lower a row when a fix lowers the count; raising one needs its reason in the commit.
# A wire holds the graphs of every module it loads, so library graphs (Carp, POSIX,
# chalk's own) are counted once per wire that loads them.
# 2026-11-20 (class-reads): corpus and probes rows re-counted after ref/blessed/reftype
# and scalar-context hash and package-array reads took a memory input (22 new probes:
# cr1-9, hs1-9, pa1-4). (The chalk rows were still c1a48dfe's then; re-counted below.)
# 2026-11-20 (wire v2, stage 1): `control-fork` is new -- a node other than an If or a
# Loop with two control successors. It counted 3 on the corpus (one graph,
# Carp::caller_info, in three wires: `$#args = N` alone in an arm) and 1 on the probes
# (cr8) before the arm scan learned what the walk pins; both are 0 and must stay 0.
# 2026-11-20 (wire v2, stage 0): the chalk rows re-counted at chalk 45a1b8d5 with this
# producer (they were c1a48dfe's, from before class reads). read-unversioned:object-class
# 4451 -> 0 and :package 17 -> 5 are the class-read work; memory-order-disagrees is 291
# where the stale row said 228, and it is 291 under the producer before this stage too
# (6d212cc): the rise is older than stage 1 and was hidden while the rows were not compared.
# control-fork 1 is Chalk::Bootstrap::Perl::Actions::SubroutineDefinition (an elsif arm in a
# foreach whose inner if builds control; not reduced yet). `#graphs` is held by the ratchet
# now, as `#wires` is: a refused sub takes its violations out of every row.
# SubroutineDefinition's fork was an elsif arm whose only store sat in a nested if's true
# arm (t/wire-an-elsif-whose-inner-if-stores-keeps-its-if.t). Every other chalk row is
# unchanged (re-counted at 315dd03 with every wire compiled).
# 2026-11-20 (wire v2, stage 3): corpus2 and probes2 are the same programs written with
# wire=2 and checked by the v2 rules (docs/plans/2026-11-20-wire-v2.md, 8.1). V1
# mem-in-not-version, V3 write-unreachable, V4 control-sink and V9 control-fork are 0 and
# held there. version-off-chain (V2) is MakeCell (a version made off the control chain)
# and one builtin version left unpinned; memory-order-disagrees (V5) is mostly what
